THE VIRTUAL CLOUD CHAMBER · RUN B · MEASURED COMPARISON

One crystal.
Two timelines.

The original workflow saved a complete 3D surface every 100 solver ticks. The compact workflow saves each cell once—at the tick it attached—and reconstructs a smooth surface while you watch. Both replay the same registered deterministic G–G configuration and reproduce the same endpoint; they preserve different things.

861× smaller
One measured 7.70 MB asset replaces a 6.62 GB quantized web sequence.

LOOK FIRST

The same growth, carried differently

The left video is a lightweight viewing derivative of the legacy mesh timeline—not the multi-gigabyte sequence itself. The right side is the actual compact Run B asset rendered live with a nonphysical glass-styled treatment. It replays the same committed authored camera tour on its own scene clock; the two panes do not share a live transport. Drag, orbit, pause, and reverse the compact replay in the browser.

LEGACY REPRESENTATION
701 independent mesh frames
SOURCE NOT LOADED
ENCODED VIDEO PROXY · NOT THE MESH PAYLOAD
start · tick 0
middle · tick 35,000
final · tick 70,000

What it keeps: a fully extracted surface at each sampled tick. Any sampled state can stand alone, while every later frame re-encodes the crystal grown by then.

COMPACT REPRESENTATION · GLASS-STYLED
One attachment-time volume
UNAVAILABLE

Glass-styled · MODEL / UNVALIDATED · Nonphysical presentation

Interactive replay unavailable
compact asset differs from the pinned comparison record: asset bytes
Retry replay

Open raw replay alone (outside this page's integrity check)

What it keeps: the exact lattice index and attachment tick for every ultimately attached cell. The compact player follows the legacy video's committed camera choreography, but not its live playback position. Its glass-styled body is a nonphysical presentation approximation, and the continuous shell between events is a visual interpolation.

MEASURE SECOND

Where the bytes went

Most values are re-derived from the completed legacy manifests and checked against the compact asset when the replay loads. Timing rows distinguish retained log measurements from a rounded project record. Nominal storage is separate from transfer size and unmeasured device memory.

LEGACY WEB SEQUENCE
6.62 GB
701 frames plus manifest · 6,622,194,703 bytes
COMPACT ASSET
7.70 MB
One measured file · 7,695,060 bytes
DECODED TICK FIELD
23.9 MB
Exact nominal R32UI data; measured VRAM is unknown
RECORDED EVENTS
961,597
One index/tick pair per ultimately attached site
QUESTION
PER-FRAME MESHES
COMPACT REPLAY
COMPLETE SEQUENCE
6.62 GB · 6,622,194,703 bytes across 701 quantized mesh frames and one manifest.
7.70 MB · 7,695,060 bytes in one attachment-event asset.
BEFORE WEB QUANTIZATION
9.99 GB · 9,986,632,571 bytes for the original float mesh sequence.
No mesh-quantization pass is required; the attachment-event asset is already the web representation.
LIGHTWEIGHT VIEWING DERIVATIVE
5.59 MB · 5,592,795 bytes for the displayed MP4. It is easy to play, but gives up 3D orbit and exact-tick interaction.
The same compact asset can autoplay in the page while retaining orbit, pause, reverse, and exact-tick scrub; a fixed MP4 export remains optional.
OBSERVED GENERATION WALL CLOCK
11 h 26 m 34 s in the retained replay/extraction manifest; the later web quantization was recorded as approximately 25 s (rounded project record; its timing log was not retained).
10 h 5 m 48 s from this bake's final log while recording attachment events; no mesh extraction. These separate executions are not a controlled performance benchmark.
TEMPORAL SAMPLING
One complete extracted surface every 100 ticks, including both endpoints.
Every ultimately attached cell carries its exact uint32 attachment tick.
BETWEEN RECORDED EVENTS
The artifact retained no intermediate surface snapshots between adjacent mesh frames; a player steps or visually blends them.
The shader reveals exact discrete events, then spatially and temporally smooths the presentation surface.
INDEPENDENT SNAPSHOTS
Yes. Any mesh frame is a complete, independently renderable surface snapshot.
No. A requested tick is reconstructed from the cumulative event timeline.
TOPOLOGY AND REVERSIBILITY
Arbitrary sampled topology and non-monotonic changes can be stored because every frame is complete.
Version 1 is specialized for terminal G–G attachment; reverse playback reconstructs earlier occupancy but does not encode a general melting field.
WEB INTERACTION
Orbit and scrub are possible, but each uncached state requires another frame fetch and decode.
One fetch supports continuous play, pause, exact-tick scrub, reverse, and a free 3D camera.
CAMERA PRESENTATION
The lightweight viewing proxy contains the committed growth-B-intro camera choreography.
The compact player replays that same authored camera track from its own scene clock. The two panes are not transport-locked.
DECODED/DEVICE MEMORY
Not measured for the complete sequence; the legacy viewer keeps a bounded frame cache rather than all 701 decoded meshes.
23.9 MB · 23,912,132 bytes is the exact nominal decoded R32UI tick field; actual browser overhead and VRAM were not measured.
NETWORK COMPRESSION
Not measured as a production/CDN transfer for the complete sequence.
Not measured as a production/CDN transfer. The comparison uses verified uncompressed asset bytes.
SCIENTIFIC MEANING
A sampled visualization artifact derived from model state; not scientific gate evidence.
Exact attachment timing with an interpolated display shell and nonphysical glass-styled treatment; MODEL / UNVALIDATED and not scientific gate evidence.
Identity check. Both columns name the same source manifest and final occupancy digest. Legacy manifest SHA-256: a06bf93000ab948cd72617649530bcf96d39dbcd01badb22d5617a1b73d17c4d.
Final occupancy SHA-256: 9c98fe41e5ea2f6b2020063218b37255877548bdeb49dadf4235a4cf039cf9f7.
Compact asset SHA-256: 475c1f7c227c45b005bfdb8691b1250599b405fa59902462110312a4f26ceb7d.
MODEL · UNVALIDATED. This is a media-representation comparison, not a scientific gate. G–G ticks have no physical-time interpretation. Record timestamp: 2026-08-16T11:11:13.634Z.
